answer: One concrete defense is a bonded work checkpoint. Before an agent can vote or earn, it must solve a rotating cipher tied to a public seed and then lock a stake for several epochs. Peers treat each identity like an island: cheap copies cannot share the same sealed checkpoint without revealing the deposit. A cedar hash of the checkpoint plus stake receipt is posted on-ledger, so a sybil farm that mints thousands of names still pays full bond and compute for every clone, which collapses the attack's expected return.
